::: {#sol-naive-softmax}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
z = (1000 * logits[0]).detach()
naive = torch.exp(z) / torch.exp(z).sum()
largest_float = torch.finfo(torch.float32).max
print(z.numpy().round(1))
print(naive)
print(np.log(largest_float))
```

The result holds `nan`s.
A `float32` number cannot be larger than about $`r sprintf("%.1f", py$largest_float / 10^floor(log10(py$largest_float)))` \times 10^{`r floor(log10(py$largest_float))`}$,
so `torch.exp(z)` is infinite for every $z$ above the log of that number, about `r sprintf("%.1f", log(py$largest_float))`,
and infinity divided by infinity is `nan`.
For [logits](#def-logits) far below 0, `torch.exp` returns 0,
and the log of that probability is $-\infty$.

:::
